description: We are a team of students from Universidad de Antioquia passionate about space sciences and their real world applications. We are experienced in aerospace software, data visualization and analysis and plan to apply this knowledge towards the creation of a solution that has an impact in society.
summary:
AgroGeo is an open-source decision-support platform that helps farmers explore crop-rotation options using NASA Earth observations, agricultural information, and explainable models. Developed for eastern Antioquia, Colombia, it combines an interactive map, five XGBoost forecasting models, and a rule-based crop-rotation planning engine.

The forecasting models estimate daily mean, minimum, and maximum temperature, precipitation, and surface soil moisture up to 60 days ahead. The planning engine then evaluates crop compatibility against agronomic requirements and generates conditional sequences that alternate botanical families. A complementary statistical climate module examines seasonal conditions, water balance, and ENSO-related variability in La Unión.

Our main innovation is the architecture connecting data acquisition, quality control, prediction, and rotation assessment while preserving each result’s source, location, date, and limitations. AgroGeo makes complex environmental information easier to explore through simple and technical views. Its intended impact is to support crop diversification, soil conservation, and resilience to changing weather and water conditions. Results remain experimental and support farmer judgment and local agronomic expertise.
details:
AgroGeo turns NASA Earth observations into understandable crop-rotation scenarios for farmers in eastern Antioquia, Colombia. It explor alternatives to repeatedcultivation while accounting for changing rainfall, temperature, and soil-water conditions.

Our working, open-source web prototype lets users explore an interactive map, select a municipality or outline a plot, and examine available forecasts and compatible crops through simple and technical views.

The system connects three complementary components:

  • Five XGBoost forecasting models predict daily mean, minimum, and maximum temperature, precipitation, and surface soil moisture up to 60 days ahead. They use NASA POWER, GPM, and SMAP observations, complemented by terrain and soil information.
  • A local statistical climate module examines seasonal conditions and ENSO-related variability in La Unión, compares environmental estimates with IDEAM station records, and calculates evapotranspiration and water balance.
  • An explainable rotation-planning engine compares forecasts with FAO ECOCROP requirements, evaluates crop compatibility, and proposes up to three conditional sequences that alternate botanical families. Its interview adapter can incorporate previous crop families and farmer exclusions.

The architecture connects Earth observations → quality-controlled inputs → predictions → agronomic assessment → understandable scenarios. Each result retains its location, period, sources, and limitations, allowing users to understand the evidence behind an alternative.

AgroGeo’s intended impact is to make NASA data useful for crop diversification, soil conservation, and climate resilience. Its scenarios support discussion between farmers and agronomists. Subsequent rotation stages require updated forecasts and validation before planting decisions.
